props.title: Impromptu

sections.content: Impromptu brilliantly captures the passionate chaos of 19th-century Romantic artists, centering on George Sand's pursuit of Frédéric Chopin. Director James Lapine transforms what could've been stuffy period drama into an electric comedy of manners, with Judy Davis embodying Sand's rebellious spirit in men's clothing. The film sits alongside Amadeus (1984) and Bright Star (2009) in bringing classical artists to vibrant life, but with a distinctly feminist edge - Sand crashes through social barriers while the more reserved Chopin recoils from her advances.

sections.content: The film excels in its treatment of artistic temperament and creation. Unlike the tortured genius tropes of Total Eclipse (1995) about Rimbaud and Verlaine, or the melodrama of Song Without End (1960) about Franz Liszt, Impromptu shows artists as fully human - brilliant but flawed, serious about their work but often absurd in their personal lives. Hugh Grant's Chopin is both genius and hypochondriac, while Julian Sands captures Liszt's rock star charisma and ego.

The film's handling of gender roles feels remarkably modern. Sand's defiance of convention echoes through later female artist biopics like Artemisia (1997) and Camille Claudel (1988). The script crackles with wit while never losing sight of the era's very real restrictions on women. Emma Thompson's supporting role as Duchess d'Antan provides a sharp contrast - a woman who follows society's rules but envies Sand's freedom. SUBHEAD: Musical Innovation in Period Films

sections.content: The film's approach to classical music proves particularly innovative. Rather than treating Chopin's compositions as mere soundtrack, Impromptu makes them integral to character development. Each piece reflects the emotional state of its players, similar to how The Piano (1993) uses its score. The practice scenes between Chopin and Sand reveal as much through music as through dialogue, while the impromptu performances give insight into each character's true nature.
